published_prior_art.cite: LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP gives one-step no-assumption posterior transition bounds and a simultaneous response-law construction.

repo_prior_art.cite: No other in-catalogue proposal concerns trajectory-conditioned Shapley extrema over one shared Markov response-row coupling.

published_prior_art.cite: ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCounterfactual gives general tight canonical-SCM polynomial programs, but not the posterior product program or shared sequential Shapley image; LeePleckoBareinboim2026ImprovingCausalExplanations remains source-verification pending.
WitterEtAl2026ExactlyDoShapley exactly compresses graph-do-Shapley by irreducible intervention classes; the beta-integral identity is standard, while this Markov posterior specialization is narrower.

repo_prior_art.cite: No catalogue entry gives an exact mixed-elimination compiler preserving one posterior response-row assignment across trajectory-Shapley branches.

published_prior_art.cite: LiuIhler2013MarginalMAP and ParkDarwiche2004MAPComplexity establish generic sum-max constraints, and ChoiFriedmanVanDenBroeck2022MarginalMAP gives exact circuit transformations, but none gives this causal shared-coupling compiler.
The verified Lally and Zhang results bound individual counterfactual queries; no verified source compares one common SCM against coalitionwise reoptimization on an open Markov family.

KaidoMolinariStoye2019CalibratedProjection treats general partially identified projections and LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP takes transition probabilities as known; neither supplies this posterior-fiber inversion.
The local posterior-cap denominator is a useful specialization, but it is an optimization-stability consequence rather than an independently established frontier.

LiLeeBareinboim2026CounterfactualShapley Assumption 3.3 selects independent response rows and its simulation rule resamples nonfactual rows, so this is a required sanity reduction rather than new prior art.

source_verification_receipts.locator: lines 103-117 (AAMAS metadata and abstract); lines 263-315 (exact closed-form MDP bounds); lines 508-517 (no-assumption row bounds)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives tight closed-form counterfactual transition bounds in Markovian MDPs and, without its optional stability/monotonicity restrictions, gives the posterior-row upper and lower formulas used as this proposal's one-step substrate.

The proceedings paper proves a finite canonical-SCM reduction for discrete counterfactual distributions and translates tight bounding into polynomial programming, while noting general computational expense.
The paper compresses interventional do-Shapley values through graph-induced irreducible-set classes and gives exact O(r(d+e+T)) computation, not posterior-conditioned shared-coupling optimization.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: After making the strict-gap family fully explicit, give its complete H=2 table: π, both policies, every selected posterior row, and direct endpoint calculations before proving the relatively open extension.

Turn the compiler OEQ into a sharper constructive target by stating the affine/sign normalization of the signed Shapley objective, explicit factor scopes, and a worked rational H=2 circuit whose backpointer produces a response-table sampler.

Add an explicit finite-sample endpoint-width bound in n_min and compare it to the robust-MDP inference benchmark of BennettKallusOprescuSunWang2024, clearly separating this partial-identification fiber from their transition-shift sensitivity model.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Li citation anchors, define the signed circuit and complete strict-gap DGP, and introduce a subclass-specific identified set Θ_i^CI; then return this angle for renewed novelty review.
